name: What happens if the replacement property in a 1031 exchange has a lower value than the relinquished property?

mainEntity.name: What happens if the replacement property in a 1031 exchange has a lower value than the relinquished property?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the replacement property in a 1031 exchange has a lower value than the relinquished property, you will receive 'boot' — non-like-kind property or cash. This 'boot' is taxable up to the amount of the gain realized on the original sale. To achieve a fully tax-deferred exchange, the investor must reinvest all the net proceeds from the sale of the relinquished property and acquire a replacement property of equal or greater value and equity. Receiving boot, such as excess cash, will trigger partial capital gains tax liability, even if the primary exchange is valid.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the replacement property has lower value, the difference, known as 'boot,' becomes taxable up to the original gain.
